I'm sure we can agree becoming a competent survivalist demands expertise in addition to being adequately equipped with tools and supplies.

I recently stumbled across a video on blacksmithing; although I wont be building a forge anytime soon, it made me wonder what other cool and useful skills I haven't thought about yet.

My efforts so far include:

  • Training as a volunteer with an emergency medical service provider.

  • Using radiocomms at my day job.

  • Independent study on living off the land, I can identify a fair few native edible plants in my area and know how to find water and yummy grubs etc.

  • A little bit of hunting: tracking, snaring and archery. (I'm vegetarian by choice so this isn't my favorite pass time, my dog loves it but she's no help.)

  • Learning to better read maps and collecting detailed topographic maps of my area.

  • Physical conditioning. I've become pretty good at walking long distance carrying weight, I wouldn't say I'm anywhere near peak physical condition though.

My plans include:

  • Continuing with the above and getting more involved in actually applying my medical training (I've worked in the field a bit but I'm not that confident and I haven't gone in a while.)

  • A formal three day survival course I've signed up for (not readily available where I live or I would have done it awhile ago).

  • Going on extended solitary hikes. I bush walk often and go camping occasionally but I want to start doing long dry runs while I have the option of sending a SOS signal if needed.

I have other vague notions of looking into animal husbandry and agriculture but they're low priority.

Any advice on how I might improve my chance of survival is more than welcome!

Edit: Ideas I've got from this sub so far that I think are worth some consideration:

  • Apiary (beekeeping).

  • Appliance repair.

  • Safe 'back-yard' abortions. (Oxymoron, I know. I hope this one doesn't get me lynched, please note this is one post-civilized skill I would NOT practice, I think it might be interesting to learn a little bit of the theory though.)

What are you doing/planning to do?

Do you know how to build a toaster from scrap metal yet or what?
What kind of training and/or study do you do regarding survivalism?

Vegetarian by choice is interesting for a survivalist. There's lots of toxic plants, and learning the difference can be really tough - but eating grubs and worms and crawly things can keep you alive for quite a while.

Haha, yeah, a lot of people are stunned that I would kill a poor cuddly bunny when I refuse to eat bacon... BACON! Even after I explain rabbits are an invasive pest and that I do it as humanely as possible (traps and snares till I'm competent in archery... I've got a long way to go there... but I can break a neck quick) I feel like they've judged me as a hypocrite/freak.

I'm not looking forward to the insects but I think you've got to be a pragmatist at heart to survive. I've got a lot of reasons I don't eat meat now but the main and most fundamental one is because my life doesn't depend on it.
